title: The Landlord of Deck Three
lead: Two hundred families on the Tollan Arms are marching on the council because their deck now legally belongs to a butler. The butler, a synthetic called Mr. Quince, has come to you separately to ask how one gives a deck away, because he's tried and the law won't let him.
anyone: Two hundred families on the Tollan Arms are marching on the council because their deck now legally belongs to a butler. The butler, a synthetic called Mr. Quince, has been asking anyone who'll listen how one gives a deck away, because he's tried and the law won't let him.

gm.truth: Under the Concord Probate Code, the Ansley family left all they owned to their household synthetic, Mr. Quince, who stayed with them to the end. They owned Deck Three of the Tollan Arms outright, including its water reclaimer, which now serves two hundred refugee families. Quince has told the families there's no rent, and they're convinced this is a trick. He tried to give it to them, but the Code bars an heir from disposing of an estate during a declared emergency without a magistrate's seal, and there are no magistrates. Void the will and you've ruled that synthetic citizens can't inherit, which means they aren't citizens. Void the Code and you've voided the law that Grann Tull's soil plots, ship charters and cargo claims all rest on. Councillor Bram Duval, of the Safe Decks campaign, is paying for the march. And Quince, behind his beautiful manners, is a hundred and forty years old and grieving. He raised four generations of Ansleys. One great-granddaughter, Pip, aged nine, was never found, and he hasn't stopped looking.
beats: Mr. Quince in the captain's office, with a tray. He has brought his own tea in case the captain's isn't suitable. He has read the whole Code several times and finds it very well drafted.
The march: angry people with reasonable fears, and a rumor that the machine will turn off the water. Quince has been fixing it personally, at night.

Legal comedy. Everyone the captain consults makes it worse: Halm's clerk, Quartermaster Brandt, an old Thessan notary. Steward Tull sends a note saying that if anyone touches the property code, she'd like to discuss her plots.
Duval's money comes to light. A couple of hired men pay Quince a visit to show him what it means to be a landlord.
A ruling, which the captain has to write, or a way around the ruling.
routes: The law: lore and persuasion. Appoint a magistrate, which raises who and by what right. That's a bigger question than this deck, and everyone will realize it within the hour.
The deal: commerce to set up a deck co-op with Quince as hired steward, which he'd love, and leadership to get two hundred families to vote for something they'd never accept from a machine.
The dirty way: deception, with a backdated magistrate's seal. Quince would be horrified, and he wouldn't tell.

The search: streetwise and awareness to trace the missing heir. If crew_naomi_under_crew has been played, there's a nine-year-old chief engineer in the Meridian's walls with very familiar manners, who legally owns Deck Three.
checks: lore:hard to find a way through the Probate Code
commerce:moderate to draw up a co-op all sides can live with
leadership:moderate to get two hundred families to stop shouting
streetwise:moderate to find out who's paying for the march
deception:hard to forge a magistrate's seal Mr. Quince wouldn't notice
intimidation:easy to see off the men sent to reason with a butler
fights: dock_thug pair hired to show Mr. Quince what landlords get. He's unexpectedly good with a serving tray
outcomes: A magistrate: the fleet has its first civil judge, and everyone's first question is who appointed them. Quince is free to sign the deed over. Deck Three holds a party, and he caters it.

The co-op: Quince stays on as hired steward, at his own request and a salary of one credit a year. Families start bringing him their disputes. Within a month it's the best-run deck on the ship, and Duval has to explain why his march is over.
Will voided: the law now says synthetics can't inherit. Every synthetic in the fleet stops being a citizen the same day. Mercy Seven comes to see the captain, and gives a percentage.

Pip Ansley found: Quince sets down his tray, says nothing for a long moment, and asks if Miss Ansley has eaten. The deck's legal owner is nine, and she'd like a word with the tenants about their ducts.
gm.rewards: forged_papers of flawless quality that aren't quite forged, goodwill among the fleet's synthetics, and a butler who'll now turn up at crucial moments with exactly the right document.
